sources.citation: Post, Mark W. 2015. 'Tones in Northeast Indian languages, with a focus on Tani: A fieldworker's guide.' In M. W. Post, S. Morey & S. DeLancey (eds.), Language and Culture in Northeast India and Beyond: In honor of Robbins Burling (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 023), ch. 11, pp. 182-210. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: First-hand (author's own 1,900-lexeme Tangam database): Tangam listed under 'Tone, confirmed' (Table 5, p.190); sec. 5.4 pp.203-204 gives H vs L minimal pairs (Table 21) and says no more than a two-way contrast; fn.11 p.204: tone interacts with syllable weight 'like in Apatani'. Nothing at all about word stress/accent placement in Tangam.
